# Automate Local Video Creation and Publishing to Instagram Reels & YouTube Shorts

## Quick overview
Coordinate local video rendering and scheduled Instagram Reels / YouTube Shorts delivery. This is an orchestration template, not an installed renderer.

## How it works
Manual drafts or a daily batch enter a durable queue. A PC worker renders the media and uploads authorized bytes. Publishing claims a ready video, completes Instagram, then verifies a YouTube upload of the original MP4.

## Setup
1. Keep this template inactive while configuring it.
2. Assign your own credentials; remove inherited account associations before sharing.
3. Install the matching external runtime and persistent storage. The JSON does not include these services.
4. Configure service URLs, helper paths, HTTPS media routes and target accounts.
5. Use fictional sample content, neutral colors and assets you own; inspect the rendered output for unwanted branding.
6. Prove preview/no-publishing behavior before authorizing any live platform test.

## Customization
Change content, layouts, schedules and timezone in their actual configuration locations. Keep authorization, validation and receipts intact.

## Publishing safety
Manual execution can reach real platform writes. Do not rely on a trigger name, dryRun flag or YouTube privateTest without validating its actual branch/backend behavior. This note does not certify runtime readiness.

## Documentation
[Setup, testing and operations](https://paoloronco.notion.site/Automate-Local-Video-Creation-and-Publishing-to-Instagram-Reels-YouTube-Shorts-41af0ba27c32817aac38f04798207385)

## 1. Manual drafts and PC review
Choose four format/audience pairs, enqueue jobs and poll their state. Review the previews on the rendering PC before publishing. The gallery's loopback URL opens on that PC only.

Retries and separate executions can create new request keys: inspect existing jobs before resubmitting. The status diagnostic is independent.

## 2. Signed worker bridge
The PC initiates requests to claim or finish jobs. n8n checks envelope structure; the external queue service must verify signatures, expiry, nonce replay and leases. Test invalid and replayed requests before exposure.

## 3. Batch and publishing schedules
The schedule requests five jobs at 09:00 and claims ready media at 10:00, 12:00, 15:00, 18:00 and 21:00.

Set the workflow timezone explicitly and review both triggers. Five slots do not guarantee five posts. Keep schedules disabled until setup and recovery checks pass.

## 4. Instagram, then YouTube
Claim a ready video, follow the helper's Instagram actions and persist results. Continue to YouTube only through the verified-Instagram gate; validate the channel and retain each upload ID before processing checks.

YouTube private visibility is not a private Instagram test. Verify helper dry-run behavior; reconcile partial success before retrying. Stream metadata is not proof of audible narration or Shorts classification.

## 5. Authorized MP4 upload
Validate the envelope, obtain backend authorization, restore the original binary and transfer only to the restricted destination. Verify the uploaded bytes before acknowledging completion. Do not remove path checks or trust a filename as file validation.

## 6. Expiring media delivery
Let the backend authorize the exact job/file and expiry before reading media. Serve only the approved MP4 with no-store headers. Signature-format checks alone are not cryptographic verification; test tampered and expired URLs.
